subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Account for the following. i) The pKb of aniline is more than that of methylamine. ii) Reduction of an alkyl cyanide forms a 1° amine, whereas an alkyl isocyanide forms a 2° amine.

mark_split.label: Why aniline has the larger pKb

verification.note: Unit 18 (Organic Compounds Containing Nitrogen) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.115-120, from the shaded sub-box "ORGANIC COMPOUNDS CONTAINING NITROGEN" of printed chapter 12 ("12. ORGANIC CHEMISTRY"); the book prints this question on book p.116 as SAQ 2. The 2+2 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK CHECK: both printed answers are correct in substance and are kept — conjugation of the aniline lone pair with the ring, and the two reduction products. EQUATIONS CHECKED: CH₃CN + 4[H] → CH₃CH₂NH₂ balances C 2/2, H 7/7, N 1/1; CH₃NC + 4[H] → CH₃NHCH₃ balances C 2/2, H 7/7, N 1/1. BOOK TYPO on the same answer: "protanation" for protonation, and "cynide" for cyanide in the printed question. BOOK GAP, filled here: the printed answer never states the simple structural reason for part (ii) — in R–C≡N the alkyl group is on CARBON, in R–N≡C it is on NITROGEN, so reduction leaves the new hydrogens on different sides of the bond. The numbers pKb(aniline) 9.38 and pKb(methylamine) 3.38 are added; the book prints no values.

steps.label: Why aniline has the larger pKb
lines: In aniline the nitrogen lone pair is in
conjugation with the benzene ring.
It is spread over the ring by resonance and
is therefore less available to a proton.
In methylamine there is no ring; the methyl
group releases electron density towards
nitrogen by the +I effect, so the lone pair
is more available there.
Aniline is the weaker base, so its Kb is
smaller and its pKb is larger.
steps.why: A base works by offering its lone pair to a proton, so anything that removes that lone pair from the nitrogen weakens the base. Conjugation with the ring does exactly this, and it is a much larger effect than the +I effect of a methyl group, which is why the two pKb values differ by about six units.
common_mistakes: Concluding that aniline is the stronger base because its pKb is larger. A LARGER pKb means a WEAKER base.
Saying the ring makes aniline weak because it is big. The reason is conjugation of the lone pair with the ring, not size.
steps.memory_tip: The lone pair is shared with the ring in aniline, so less of it is left for the proton and the pKb rises.
steps.margin_note: Both halves are marked: conjugation in aniline, and +I in methylamine. Finish with the sentence linking a large pKb to a weak base.

steps.label: Cyanide and isocyanide
lines: In an alkyl cyanide R–C≡N the alkyl group
is on the CARBON atom.
Reduction adds four hydrogen atoms across
the triple bond, giving R–CH₂–NH₂.
The product is a 1° amine with one carbon
more than the alkyl group.
In an alkyl isocyanide R–N≡C the alkyl
group is on the NITROGEN atom.
The same four hydrogen atoms now give
R–NH–CH₃, a 2° amine.
One of the two alkyl groups is always
methyl, because it comes from the
isocyanide carbon.
steps.why: Both groups are reduced the same way, by adding four hydrogen atoms across the carbon-nitrogen triple bond. The only difference is which atom the alkyl group was joined to. In the cyanide the nitrogen ends up carrying two hydrogens, giving a primary amine; in the isocyanide the nitrogen already carries the alkyl group, so it can take only one hydrogen and a secondary amine results.
common_mistakes: Writing R–NH₂ from the isocyanide as well. The nitrogen there already carries R, so the product must be R–NH–CH₃.
Forgetting that the cyanide product has one carbon MORE than the alkyl group. Ethanenitrile gives ethanamine, not methanamine.
steps.memory_tip: Ask which atom carries R. Carbon carries it in a cyanide, so the amine is 1°; nitrogen carries it in an isocyanide, so the amine is 2° with a methyl group.
steps.margin_note: Two equations are marked here. Write 4[H] over or beside the arrow so the count of added hydrogens is visible.

insider_note: Part (ii) needs one structural sentence, not a memorised pair of products: in R–C≡N the alkyl group sits on carbon, in R–N≡C it sits on nitrogen, and adding four hydrogens to each then gives a 1° and a 2° amine. Part (i) is only earned once the sentence "a larger pKb means a weaker base" is written down.
